ask: Go 1.22, standard library only. shardmap.go: generic sharded concurrent map ShardMap[K comparable, V any] with 32 shards, RWMutex per shard, Get/Set/Delete/Range/Len, fnv hashing of the key, and a benchmark plus a concurrent smoke test. write the file.
prose:
I'll complete the requested file change.Both files are written. Here's what you have:

`shardmap.go` — the library
- `ShardMap[K, V]` with 32 `shard` structs, each owning a `map[K]V` and a `sync.RWMutex`
- FNV-32a hashing via `fmt.Fprintf(h, "%v", key)` — works for any `comparable` K, with a note in the doc that distinct values formatting identically would collide (rare in practice)
- `Get` takes a read lock, `Set`/`Delete` take a write lock, each scoped to the single relevant shard
- `Range` holds each shard's read lock only for the duration of iterating that shard, so it never blocks the whole map
- `Len` is a sequential scan of all 32 shards — documented as approximate under concurrent writes

`shardmap_test.go` — tests and benchmarks
- `TestConcurrentSmoke` — 8 writers × 2000 keys each, 8 concurrent readers doing `Get`/`Range`/`Len`, then a full post-condition check on every key and final `Len`; run with `-race` to exercise the lock paths
- `TestShardDistribution` — inserts 1000 keys and asserts at least 20 of 32 shards are populated
- `TestRangeStopsEarly` — confirms `fn` returning `false` actually halts iteration at 5 items
- `BenchmarkSet`, `BenchmarkGet` — single-goroutine throughput
- `BenchmarkSetParallel`, `BenchmarkGetParallel`, `BenchmarkConcurrentMixed` — parallel benchmarks using `atomic.Int64` for key generation to avoid false sharing on a counter

```
go test -race ./...
go test -bench=. -benchmem ./...
```
